child.text: Hello, it's Didgee. And here's Pebble.
Grown up, come and sit close. This one is about bedtime, and it is a cosy one.
Let's breathe together. Breathe in, and blow out slowly, like cooling a cup of warm milk.
One more. In. And out. Lovely.
Last time, we learned that someone made everything on a screen. Today, it's something everybody does, every single night.
Today's special words are wind down.
Winding down is the slow, quiet bit before sleep. Like a toy that slows down, and slows down, and stops.
When you sleep, your body gets the rest it needs.
That is why everybody needs sleep. Grown ups too. And Pebble. Pebble needs a lot.
Screens are fun. They are bright, and busy, and exciting.
And exciting things make it hard for your brain to wind down. Even when you are really tired.
Pause me here, and ask each other the question. I'll wait.
So here is our bedtime rule. Ready?
Screens go to bed first.
The tablet goes to its own bed. Not in your bedroom. In its special spot.
And look. The grown up's phone goes to bed too. Screens go to bed first. Everybody's.
Oh, Pebble. The book does not go to bed.
The book comes with us. Books are for bedtime.
Then it's time for three cosy things. Teeth. Story. Cuddle.
Your three cosy things might be different. A song, a bath, a chat about your day. You and your grown up can pick.
Pause me here, and choose your three together. Take your time.
Sometimes, at bedtime, something you saw on a screen gets stuck in your head.
If that happens, you can always tell your grown up. Even in the night.
You will never be in trouble for telling.
Let's practise. Grown up, you say: it's nearly bedtime.
And then the little one answers: screens go to bed first.
Let's try it now. Pause me if you need to.
So. We wind down before sleep. Screens go to bed first. Then, three cosy things.
Tonight, put the tablet to bed in its spot, and do your three cosy things.
Goodnight, Pebble. Goodbye from Didgee. See you next time.

parent.text: It's ten o'clock, and the light under the door is still on.
The trouble is, nothing on a screen ever finishes.
The next episode starts on its own. The game wants one more go. A tired child against that isn't a fair fight.
So take the fight away. Tonight, pick one spot outside the bedroom where every screen sleeps. Yours too.
In Guided Childhood, bedtime is protected time. No star can buy it. And if they ask anyway, the ask comes to you, not a flat no.
Here are the words to say. Phones go to bed first in our house. Mine too.
parent.big: Phones go to bed first in our house. Mine too.

parent.text: Then watch the bedtime film together. It only takes a few minutes, and your child hears the same rule in their own way.
And if they ever tell you something from a screen is stuck in their head, thank them for telling you. That is the night it matters most.
parent.eye: If something is stuck in their head

hook: One bedtime rule a five year old can say back
book_line: Screens go to bed first. A few minutes, on the sofa.

ask1: Older child: What is the last thing you do before you go to sleep?
ask2: What shall our three cosy things be?
Older child: Where shall the screens sleep in our house?
